title: Build a budget-aware Jev bot
description: Estimate a Jev bot's full running cost, route expensive analysis only when warranted, and validate decision thresholds before automating actions.

source.title: Jev Bot: The AI That Has to Pay for Its Own Brain

guide_authors.name: Appit Studio
guide_authors.role: Editorial guide; AI-assisted drafting and technical review

connections.step: Estimate complete Jev request size before a bounded replay
connections.why: The independent Python encoder estimates input tokens for structured state and all questions together, so the article's one-thought cost can be tested against the proposed request rather than a bare text length.
connections.limitations: MIT Python 3.10+ source; local estimates need no TypeSafe key and send no data. Its reconstructed Jev 1.13 encoder is not a provider billing guarantee. Recheck against response.usage.input_tokens after model changes; live provider calls carry separate charges. Paone did not mention or endorse this project.

connections.step: Compare labeled outcomes and review thresholds offline
connections.why: The provider-neutral Python CLI evaluates recorded probabilities and user-supplied mistake and hand-off costs. It can help check a candidate gate, while the application still owns the budget, actions and outcome log.
connections.limitations: Apache-2.0 Python 3.10+ CLI. Offline reports need labeled decisions and honest cost inputs, not a TypeSafe key; no inference is performed. Synthetic demos do not establish calibration for a bot or trading edge. It does not fit a calibrator, debit a wallet or execute a policy. Paone did not mention or endorse this project. Its confidence input must have a defined correctness-probability meaning; preserve raw TypeSafe confidence separately and evaluate any fitted mapping on held-out cases. Its Choice normalizer overrides a supplied confidence from a probabilities map; keep raw distributions outside fitted report rows.

faqs.question: How much does a Jev bot cost per day?
faqs.answer: At one 1,000-input-token Jev call per second and TypeSafe's listed $0.042 per million input tokens, the Jev inference estimate is $3.63 per day. Add hosting, larger-model calls, retries, data, reviews, transaction fees and mistakes separately; measure actual usage before budgeting.

faqs.question: Does a $65 budget let a Jev bot run for 18 days?
faqs.answer: Only in the article's model-only scenario: one 1,000-input-token Jev call each second at the listed rate. The calculation omits hosting and every other cost, and it does not show revenue or a live 18-day run.

faqs.question: Can Jev confidence decide when a bot should trade?
faqs.answer: No raw confidence value proves that a trade is correct or profitable. Choice confidence summarizes the option distribution; a threshold needs task-specific labeled outcomes, a held-out check and code-owned risk limits. Keep trading disabled in the pilot.

faqs.question: What happens when a Jev budget or service fails?
faqs.answer: Stop paid calls before the reserved budget is exhausted, record the reason and leave the item for review. An unavailable, malformed or late model answer must not become an automatic action; reconcile estimated charges with provider usage when service returns.
